lessons.title: Add supports and loads
lessons.question: Where does the force enter, and what is allowed to move?
lessons.goal: Select actual grid nodes, constrain the left edge and apply one total downward force of 100 N.
steps: Continue your saved lesson 02 definition, or open the partly wired starter. Open the shared Rhino model in millimetres and keep h = 6 mm.
Right-click Fixed edge → Set one Curve; select the vertical curve on layer 02_Fixed_edge. Right-click Load point → Set one Point; select the point on 03_Load_point.
Add TopOpt Support and TopOpt Load if continuing your own file. In the supplied starter they are already placed. Feed Domain / D to the D input of both.
Connect Fixed edge to Support / Selection (G). Connect Load point to Load / Selection (G). These two selection wires are deliberately absent in the starter.
Keep Support Fix X and Fix Y true. These are translations along the domain plane axes; World XY is used here.

Use the supplied vector parameter (0, -100, 0). Connect it to Load / Total force (F). In a file built by hand, right-click a Vector parameter → Set one Vector, or construct XYZ with X = 0, Y = -100, Z = 0.
Inspect Support / Nodes and Load / Nodes in Rhino. Add native Point parameters as viewers if needed. Confirm the left edge and the midpoint of the right edge.
Read the messages: Support selects 11 nodes; Load selects 1 node. The force is TOTAL, not 100 N per selected node.
Hide the illustrative arrow layer if it causes confusion. The reference arrow is not a numerical load. Save the file for lesson 04.
checkpoint: h = 6 mm; 200 active cells.
Left-edge support: 11 nodes, both X and Y fixed.
Right midpoint load: 1 node, total force (0, -100, 0) N.
You can distinguish the geometry selection, snapped nodes and applied force.

Only selected node translations are constrained. The rest of the plate can deform.

lessons.title: Run the first FEM analysis
lessons.question: Does the calculated response agree with your prediction?
lessons.goal: Run a full-material baseline, check equilibrium and distinguish numerical displacement from its display scale.
steps: Continue the supported/loaded plate from lesson 03, or use the starter. Set Boundary, Fixed edge and Load point from the same Rhino model if the parameters are empty.
Keep h = 6 mm, a 100 N downward load and the left edge fixed. Do not change the geometry between stages of the comparison.
Inspect TopOpt Material: steel Preset = 0, Length unit = 0 (mm), Force unit = 0 (N), Stock thickness = 2 mm. Its E output should be 210,000 N/mm² and nu = 0.30.

Read Engineering Settings: Backend = 0 (CPU direct), Thickness = 2 mm, Volume = 0.40, Iterations = 80, Radius = 1.8 cells, Threshold = 0.40, Keep attachments = true. The baseline uses the full active domain; Volume controls the later optimisation.
Connect Load L → Load Case Loads (L), name “Downward 100 N”, Weight = 1. This is the missing wire in the starter. One case contains the loads acting together.
Trace Domain D, Support S, Load Case Case, Material M and Settings O into the corresponding inputs of the Engineering component labelled BASELINE. Confirm Mode = 0.
Use a momentary RUN BASELINE button pulse, then wait for completed status. Opening the file does not start a solve. Do not repeatedly press Run while a job is active.
Feed the baseline Result R to FEM Results. First use Field = 1 (displacement) and Scale = 0, then Scale = 1. Increase Scale for visibility, noting that this changes the drawing only.
Read FEM Results Info and its U/Reac outputs. The maximum displacement should be about 0.009277 mm. Sum reaction vectors: total Y is approximately +100 N, balancing -100 N applied.
Switch Field = 0 or 2 for von Mises stress. Record units and the legend maximum, not only the colour. Save the definition and note the job folder. Take the scheduled 10-minute break after this block.
checkpoint: Completed full-material FEM, not an optimisation preview.
Declared units mm and N; E = 210,000 N/mm², nu = 0.30, t = 2 mm.
Displacement ≈ 0.009277 mm; total reaction Y ≈ +100 N.
Scale changes display only; you can state one modelling assumption.
problems: No response after opening
Connect the inputs, allow the initial Grasshopper solution, then pulse Run. Buttons start jobs; opening a file does not.
Old result disappears
Changing a solver input makes the old result stale. Stop/Reset if needed, then rerun the changed problem.
Unstable/singular model
Return to the selected nodes and constrained directions. A colour map cannot repair missing restraints.
Deformation looks huge
Read the numerical U value and display Scale. Scale = 1 means actual displacement.
Red stress means failure?
Auto-scaled red is the current maximum, not a pass/fail criterion. Read numbers, units and assumptions.

lessons.notes:
For the teaching sequence we use Engineering, Mode 0 rather than the minimal FEM Analyze component. This keeps the baseline compatible with optimisation, final verification and Compare Results. FEM Results is still the 2D field viewer. The standalone FEM Analyze workflow is available in the reference but is not a substitute baseline for Compare Results.

The 2 mm stock declaration informs material reference screening; Settings Thickness defines the physical FEM thickness. Neither value changes the Rhino outline. Density is used for mass; gravity is absent in this introductory problem.

Reference: full-plate mass 0.113040 kg, maximum von Mises stress about 10.558 MPa at this grid. Peak stress has not been established as mesh-converged. This lesson does not set a project-specific acceptance limit.

lessons.title: Optimise the structure
lessons.question: Where should a limited amount of material remain?
lessons.goal: Run a density optimisation with a fixed material budget and explain the objective, filter and termination reason.
steps: Continue the completed lesson 04 model or open the starter and select the shared Rhino geometry. Rerun BASELINE if this file has no current result; runtime results are not embedded in the teaching archive.
Keep geometry, h = 6 mm, supports, load, units and thickness unchanged. Use CPU direct for this small classroom model.
Inspect Settings: Volume = 0.40, Iterations = 80 (maximum), Radius = 1.8 cells (10.8 mm at h = 6), Threshold = 0.40, Keep attachments = true. No manufacturing symmetry or extrusion is imposed.
Trace the new Engineering component labelled OPTIMISATION. It receives the same D, S, Cases and M as BASELINE, but Mode = 1. Connect Settings O → OPTIMISATION O; this wire is missing in the starter.
Feed OPTIMISATION Result R to TopOpt Results. Use Field = 0 for density, Threshold T = 0.40 and Deformation scale S = 0. Hide baseline preview while viewing the design.
Pulse RUN OPTIMISATION once. Observe progress and wait for a completed result. Read the termination reason in Status/Info: completed alone does not establish convergence or feasibility.
Read the continuous-density material fraction and compliance. With this exact reference setup, optimisation converges; reference mass is 0.045216 kg and maximum displacement about 0.046659 mm.

Compare mass and deformation with the full-material baseline. Optimisation improves the starting 40%-density distribution; its “improvement” percentage is not a stiffness gain over the full-solid plate.
For one controlled optional variation, try Volume = 0.50 and rerun the design. Record the changed input and response, then restore 0.40 and rerun before lesson 06.
Save the definition and retain the completed optimisation job folder. The threshold mesh is a candidate shape; do not treat its density response as a verified binary part.

Radius is in cells. At h = 6 mm, Radius 1.8 corresponds to 10.8 mm.

Domain K is only explicit keep geometry. Engineering can additionally preserve cells touching support and point-load nodes.

lessons.notes:
Compliance is load times displacement summed over the loaded degrees of freedom; lower compliance means a stiffer response for the same loading. The objective here is stiffness under a material budget, not an automatic proof of strength or constructability.

The reference density design retains 40% of full mass. Material near load/support interfaces is preserved by Engineering even though the Domain message reports 0 explicitly kept cells. This distinction matters when comparing interfaces and volume budgets.

The minimal TopOpt Solver can also optimise a single simultaneous load set. This course uses Engineering so the same result can be used in Mode 2 and compared against its baseline. Do not mix an unrelated simple-Solver result into the Engineering Source input.

lessons.title: Extract and check the shape
lessons.question: Does the extracted shape still carry the load?
lessons.goal: Convert densities into a binary cell shape, run a new FEM solve and compare it against the matching baseline.
steps: Continue lesson 05 or open the starter. Select the shared Rhino geometry, then run BASELINE and OPTIMISATION in that order if the file has no current results.
Keep the same physical model. In Settings, Threshold = 0.40; connect that same value to the optimisation Results T input. Use Scale = 0 to inspect the candidate without display distortion.
Read Results Shape M. It retains cells whose density is at least 0.40. This mesh is not a new structural analysis.
Trace the third Engineering component labelled VERIFICATION. D, S, Cases, M and O match the earlier stages; Mode = 2.
Connect the completed OPTIMISATION Result R → VERIFICATION Source. This is the missing wire in the starter. Source expects engineering result data, not the mesh from Shape M.
Pulse RUN VERIFICATION after optimisation completes. Wait for a completed binary-grid reanalysis. Read errors rather than forcing a disconnected candidate through.
Connect the verified result to FEM Results and inspect displacement and stress. The binary candidate uses full material in retained cells; it is not smoothed or remeshed.
Compare Results receives BASELINE Result R as Baseline and VERIFICATION Result R as Candidate. Read its mass saving and displacement comparison. Matching inputs and completed results are required.

Reference at T = 0.40: mass 0.0542592 kg, maximum displacement about 0.0186599 mm, maximum von Mises about 20.3149 MPa. It is 52% lighter than the full plate; its mass differs from the 40%-density design.

Optional challenge after recording the reference: set the shared threshold to 0.50 and run VERIFICATION again. The supplied reference design produces disconnected pieces and is rejected. Record this as a modelling observation, then restore 0.40 and rerun verification.
Save the model and report locations. If baking Shape M, use an explicit Bake pulse, label the Rhino geometry as a thresholded candidate and test Undo. Bake does not validate the structure.

Continuous density and binary thresholding are different material distributions; new stiffness and mass are expected.

lessons.notes:
The phrase final verification here means full-material FEM on the retained binary grid. It does not mean verification of a smooth CAD redesign, a manufactured specimen or a structural system. A later geometry edit would require its own model and analysis.

For a refinement study, hold the physical shape and loads fixed. Rerunning optimisation on a finer grid changes the design as well as the discretisation. Point-load and sharp-corner peak stresses need particular care.

lessons.title: Apply the workflow to the roof rib
lessons.question: Can the same sequence explain an architectural case?
lessons.goal: Recognise the existing three-stage workflow, inspect five independent cases and explain a change in support reactions.
steps: Open the prepared roof Grasshopper model from the shared examples. Geometry is internalised; use the optional roof Rhino file for orientation, not as a required external selection.
Locate Domain, Keep regions, supports, Material, Settings, the five Load Cases and the three calculation stages. Do not rebuild the entire roof definition in this 25-minute transfer exercise.
Confirm the reference setup: span 6,000 mm; heel 300 mm plus rise 1,500 mm; thickness 12 mm; h = 100 mm; 630 active cells and 44 explicit Keep cells.
Read the supports: left pin fixes X/Y; right anchored roller fixes Y and allows X. These are bilateral restraints and can develop hold-down tension under uplift.
Inspect each named Load Case. Loads inside one case act together, including self-weight. Different cases are solved independently. Objective weight 1 is not a load factor.

Check Gravity in World XY: cases 1 and 5 use (0, -9.80665, 0) m/s²; ULS snow cases 2–4 use 1.3g = (0, -12.748645, 0) m/s². X and Z are zero. Acceleration units are always m/s², while point loads here are in N.

If time permits, run 01 BASELINE FEM → 02 OPTIMISATION → 03 FINAL VERIFICATION, waiting for completion between stages. Otherwise use the supplied reference table for the discussion and label it as reference evidence.
Use Review Stage 0/1/2 to display baseline/design/verification. Stage changes the visible result, not which solver is run. Use Case 1–5 only after completion to inspect saved case responses.

Use Field = 1 for displacement or Field = 2 for stress. Field 0 means FEM stress in stages 0/2, but design density in stage 1. Set a shared positive legend maximum for comparisons of the same physical field.
Read the final SLS displacement and the wind-uplift reactions. Explain why a lighter plate may require greater downward hold-down force.
Choose one controlled group variation only if time remains. Record the changed parameter; do not mix its result into the supplied reference table as though it were the same model.
checkpoint: You identified five independent cases and the three calculation stages.
You distinguished thickness, cell size and tributary spacing.
You can explain the sign of uplift reactions.
You label supplied values as reference unless you reproduced them.
problems: Case selector fails
Wait for completed stage and keep its job folder in place; selection reads saved case files.
Changing Stage does not run a solve
Review is a display control. Use the stage’s Run button to calculate.
Unexpected uplift reactions
The roller is anchored/bilateral in this model. Downward reaction means a hold-down demand, not loss of contact automatically.
Default Gravity points out of plane
Use the supplied negative-Y vector for XY. Cases 1 and 5 use -9.80665 m/s²; ULS snow cases 2–4 use -12.748645 m/s². X and Z are zero; the generic default points along -Z.
A 25-minute roof analysis takes too long
Use the embedded reference table and focus on interpretation. Do not claim that a reference run is a student-produced result.

lessons.notes:
This is a short transfer exercise adapted from the repository’s existing roof course. The supplied actions and combination coefficients are fixed teaching assumptions, not site-specific design inputs. No new regulation review is implied.

The six roof stations each represent 3 m² of horizontal tributary area. The SLS teaching force is -(0.15 + 0.60 + 0.80) × 3 = -4.65 kN per station; convert to -4,650 N for the model. Full-plate self-weight is about 5.81985 kN, giving about +16.85993 kN vertical reaction at each support under the symmetric SLS case.

At the reference h = 100 mm, Volume = 0.30 and Threshold = 0.40. Filter radius is 180 mm, entered as 180/h = 1.8 cells. Reference optimisation converged after 36 iterations. Refining the same binary shape to 50 and 25 mm raises peak stress substantially; this sequence does not demonstrate converged peak stress.

lessons.title: Discuss the results
lessons.question: What can you defend using the evidence you collected?
lessons.goal: Present a concise comparison, distinguish observed results from reference values and propose a justified next check.
steps: Open your saved model and worksheet notes. Use the small plate comparison as the common minimum; add the roof observations if you completed them.
Choose the full-material baseline and the verified binary candidate from the same physical model. Do not compare an unrelated job or relaxed design stress as though it were binary FEM stress.
Record geometry, units, material, h, thickness, applied force, threshold and which stages you actually ran. If you used reference values, label them explicitly.
Present mass and maximum displacement for both stages, plus termination and verification status. Use matching field units, legend maximum and deformation scale for visual comparisons.
Explain one difference between your lesson 01 prediction and the calculated response. A changed understanding is a useful outcome.
State one unresolved modelling issue and one concrete next check. Examples: loading/support patches, fixed-shape refinement, out-of-plane stability or a connection model.
Save your Grasshopper definition, the completed worksheet or PDF, and your observation table. Keep the runtime job folder if you need case selection and report access later.
Give a 30-second evidence-based conclusion to your partner. End with what you would investigate next, rather than declaring the part universally safe.

lessons.notes:
Suggested minimum submission: saved Grasshopper definition; completed worksheet/PDF; a baseline-versus-verified comparison with units; and a four-sentence conclusion. Keep reference files unchanged and save personal work under a new name.

Assessment: model and units (5 points), correct stages and numerical evidence (5), controlled comparison and interpretation (5), limitations and reproducible communication (5). Do not grade visual smoothness as proof of accuracy.
